proposals.before: In 1862 Li Hongzhang led eight thousand Huai Army men to Shanghai, and Songlin went with him. West of the city he fought the rebel kings Li Xiucheng and Tan Shaoguang and routed a rebel host of one hundred thousand.
proposals.after: In 1862 Li Hongzhang led eight thousand Huai Army men to Shanghai, and Songlin went with him. West of the city he fought the rebel Loyal King Li Xiucheng and the rebel Prince Mu Tan Shaoguang and routed a rebel host of one hundred thousand.
proposals.reason: 偽慕王 is Prince Mu (慕王), not a vague 'Princely King'; 偽忠王 is Loyal King. The idiomatic gloss collapses both titles.

proposals.before: In 1861 Anqing fell; he was promoted to battalion commander and given the title Brave Baturu.
proposals.after: In 1861 Anqing fell; he was promoted to major (youji) and given the title Brave Baturu.
proposals.reason: 游擊 is the Qing rank youji (major), not a modern 'battalion commander'.

proposals.before: In 1856 he joined Zeng Guoquan's forces, marched to relieve Jiangxi, took Anfu, and helped clear Yongxin, Taihe, Wan'an, Lianhua subprefecture, and Longquan, for which he was commended and given the rank of corporal.
proposals.after: In 1856 he joined Zeng Guoquan's forces, marched to relieve Jiangxi, took Anfu, and helped clear Yongxin, Taihe, Wan'an, Lianhua subprefecture, and Longquan, for which he was commended and given the rank of file leader (batotal).
proposals.reason: 把總 is a Qing junior officer rank (batotal), not the modern Western 'corporal'.

proposals.before: He took Zhelin, Fengxian, Nanhui, Chuansha, and Jinshan, raised the siege of Songjiang, recovered Qingpu, and was promoted to sergeant.
proposals.after: He took Zhelin, Fengxian, Nanhui, Chuansha, and Jinshan, raised the siege of Songjiang, recovered Qingpu, and was promoted to company officer (qianzong).
proposals.reason: 千總 is a Qing company-grade officer rank (qianzong), not the modern Western 'sergeant'.

proposals.before: He pressed the campaign against Changzhou, relieved Major General Tang Diankui at Benniu, and broke the siege there.
proposals.after: He pressed the campaign against Changzhou, relieved Brigade General (zongbing) Tang Diankui at Benniu, and broke the siege there.
proposals.reason: 總兵 is better rendered as brigade general / zongbing; 'Major General' is an approximate but anachronistic gloss.

proposals.before: In 1852 he enlisted, first under Li Mengqun, judicial commissioner of Hubei. When Hanyang fell he was promoted to corporal.
proposals.after: In 1852 he enlisted, first under Li Mengqun, judicial commissioner of Hubei. When Hanyang fell he was promoted to file leader (batotal).

proposals.after: In 1858 he fought at Hukou and was promoted to company officer (qianzong).
proposals.reason: 千總 is a Qing company-grade officer rank, not modern Western 'sergeant'.

proposals.after: He took the rebel stronghold at Chigang Ridge outside Anqing and was made major (youji).

proposals.after: He also helped take the Sanhe garrison outside Hefei and raise the siege of Lu'an, and was commended as company officer (qianzong).

decisions.reason: The source supplies distinct Taiping titles for both men; retaining Loyal King and Prince Mu is more informative than collapsing them to generic rebel kings.

sourceWitness.excerpt: He fought the rebel Loyal King Li Xiucheng and Prince Mu Tan Shaoguang.

decisions.after: In 1861 Anqing fell; he was promoted to colonel and given the title Brave Baturu.
decisions.reason: Youji is rendered as colonel throughout this volume's established Qing rank ladder; major would introduce a new and lower equivalent.

decisions.after: In 1856 he joined Zeng Guoquan's forces, marched to relieve Jiangxi, took Anfu, and helped clear Yongxin, Taihe, Wan'an, Lianhua subprefecture, and Longquan, for which he was commended and given the rank of platoon officer.
decisions.reason: Bazong is rendered as platoon officer in the surrounding Draft History of Qing chapters; 'corporal' is too low and 'file leader (batotal)' is needlessly obscure.
